_______________________________________________________ Hon'ble Shri Justice P. Sam Koshy Order on Board [16/01/2023]
1. Challenge in the present Writ Petition is to the Award passed by Respondent No.6 on 6.6.2022, in respect of acquisition of land belonging to the Petitioner that situates at Khasra No.608/1, 608/3,
608/4, 608/6, 608/7, admeasuring area 0.922, 0.922, 0.922, 0.761, 0.721 hectare respectively, in Village Basantpur, Tahsil Dabhra, District Sakti.
2.

Considering the fact that the substantive relief that the Petitioner seeks for in the present Writ Petition is for the quantification of the compensation awarded by the Respondent Authorities, this Court is of the opinion that it would not be justified for the Writ Court to exercise the powers of the Appellate Authority and revisit the Award as an Appellate Authority while exercising the Writ jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.

3. The appropriate remedy available to the Petitioner would be that of preferring an Appeal for challenging the said Award, under Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency Abhayram Patel vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 16 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40918208/
1 in Land Acquisition (Rehabilitation and Resettlement) Act, 2013.

sentences.text: 4. Learned Counsel for Petitioner at this juncture submits that they may be permitted to withdraw the present Writ Petition with liberty to avail the said remedy under Section 64 of the aforesaid Act.
5. The Writ Petition accordingly stands disposed of as withdrawn.

In case the Petitioner prefers an Appeal, the Appellate Authority may consider the limitation aspect taking into consideration the period spent by the Petitioner before the High Court while pursuing the present Writ Petition.
6. The Writ Petition accordingly stands disposed of.
